title: The generic orbitGraph loop (values beyond 2^53) can report truncated for a search that ends with exactly cap positions and the whole suite stays green (surviving M14 on the second search loop)
location: packages/engine/src/search.ts:320 (the generic loop's final return); packages/engine/test/unit/mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts:313-356 (the handover cases never end with exactly cap items)
claim: Since the residual fix for P3-RT-07-02, orbitGraph has two search loops. The suite pins the cap boundary of SPEC 5.5 only on the search on numbers (F10, the fast-path M14, is caught). The generic loop, which runs once a value leaves the safe range, can say truncated true at the natural end of a search with exactly cap items, and no test notices.
expected: SPEC 5.5: the cap acts only 'when the search is about to add one position more than the cap'. A search that finds exactly cap positions ends with truncated false on either loop, and some test runs the generic loop at cap equal to the orbit size.
observed: With redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch applied, `npx vitest run --project engine` exits 0 (65 files, 2218 tests). The full `npm test` set gives 133 files passing. The other two files, T03.test.ts and T11.test.ts, hit Vitest's 5 s limit at load 12 and pass when rerun under the patch (exit 0). The proposed test packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts fails 2 of 2 under the patch and passes without it. It runs A2, B2, G2 and A3 orbits and triangle layer bounds with the seeds times 2^60 against the same search on the plain seeds, at cap n-1, n and n+1.
reproduction: From this branch (b9b8504 plus dfb1716) after `npm ci --prefer-offline`: `patch -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch && npx vitest run --project engine --exclude '**/redteam-*'; echo exit=$?` gives exit=0. Then `npx vitest run --project engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts; echo exit=$?` gives exit=1. `patch -R -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch` and the same file passes.
specRef: SPEC.md 5.5 'Order and truncation of a search'; RT-11 attack 31 (surviving M14 is major); SPEC 7.7 Engine golden row; CONTRACTS.md 3
proposedFix: Adopt redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts, which compares the generic loop on scaled seeds with the search on numbers on the plain seeds at the cap boundary. Also add a cap equal to the orbit size to the handover cases of mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 5.5 'Order and truncation of a search': 'The cap acts when the search is about to add one position more than the cap: it stops at once with truncated true and exactly cap items' (unlabelled, no qualifier). This supports the finding's expected. Oracle lie_games.orbit_graph_capped(C, seeds, mutate, cap) on seeds times 2^60 gives truncated False at cap equal to the orbit size.
refute.evidence: I read everything at b9b8504 (the worktree is detached there and clean). SPEC 5.5 has no 'may', no [D] mark and no clause that limits the rule to some arithmetic. E-2 puts every non-finite and custom board on Big because entries pass 2^53, so values beyond 2^53 are a specified case. search.ts:289-298: on a SafeInt or Big board, orbitGraph first runs searchOnNumbers. Its doc comment says a seed that is not a safe integer 'hands over at once'. Lines 300-320 are the generic loop, and line 320 returns truncated false. F3 (read as text from worktree-agent-a19febfb0f4c5a241:redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch) changes that line to truncated: items.length >= cap. That is not an equivalent mutant (RT-11 section 6), because the generic loop can end naturally with exactly cap items. Oracle, run with python3 -I on copies of reference/ from b9b8504, using positions: L.orbit_graph_capped(L.cartan('A',2), units times 2^60, L.mutate, 6) gives 6 items, truncated False, complete_layers 2 (cap 5 gives True). B2 at cap 8, G2 at cap 12 and A3 at cap 12 all give False. The triangle [[2,-1,-1],[-1,2,-1],[-1,-1,2]] from [2^60,0,0] gives False at maxDepth 3, 6 and 10 with cap 18, 39 and 63. So the oracle backs the finding's expected and contradicts the mutant. mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts:330-355 (// regression: P3-RT-07-02) has these handover cases: [[2,-4],[-4,2]] and the others at cap 2000 with maxDepth 60; A2 with seeds [2^60,-2^59] and [1,0] at cap 50, which has at most 12 items; and the 12-cycle cases, which are on the fast path. None ends with exactly cap items. The other cap-boundary tests (p1-search 'triangle with a cap of 9', p3a-orbit-size) use small values, so they run the fast path. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4) records the two loops and claims equivalence on 'values past 2^53', but records no exemption for the cap boundary. gate-G4.md (4e3e839, which names b9b8504) has no open item on this, and nothing in round1-deferred.json or the P4 'known and decided' list covers it.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 5.5 has no permitting clause for any arithmetic; R2 failed, because the finding reads 5.5 correctly and an exact-cap natural end is not truncated; R3 failed, because orbitGraph is phase 1 and E-2's Big boards exist at G4; R4 failed, because the oracle gives truncated False at cap equal to the orbit size on seeds times 2^60 (A2 cap 6, triangle maxDepth 3 cap 18), so it backs the expected and not the mutant; R5 failed, because 5.5 is not [D] and the residual-perf fragment records no exemption; R6 failed, because there is no open record and the P3-RT-07-02 regression test never ends a handover search at exactly cap; the major level matches RT-11 attack 31 (a surviving M14 is major) and round 1's handling of surviving mutants.

title: The 25 ms orbit benchmark of SPEC 7.6 no longer measures Big arithmetic: the bigint loop can become 30 times slower and orbit.bench.ts stays green
location: packages/engine/test/bench/orbit.bench.ts:38-64 (seeds 0 and 1 on a Big board); packages/engine/src/search.ts:289-297 (searchOnNumbers taken on every SafeInt or Big board while values are safe)
claim: The residual fix for P3-RT-07-02 made orbitGraph search on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer. The SPEC 7.6 benchmark, '2000 positions on a board with 12 nodes in Big arithmetic', still seeds 0 and 1 and so now times the numbers path. The bigint loop with decimal keys, which it timed at G3 (19.75 to 21.60 ms, and 21.01 ms at the gate, per DECISIONS.md), now runs only for values beyond 2^53, and nothing times it. No decisions entry records this change of what the benchmark measures.
expected: SPEC 7.6 'Main-thread work': the worst case of E-9, 2000 positions on a 12-node board in Big arithmetic, is repeated by a Vitest benchmark that fails above 25 ms (median of seven). RT-11 attack 24 requires that 'the arithmetic is Big and not SafeInt or number'.
observed: redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch adds 20 microseconds to each move of the bigint loop only. Under it, orbit.bench.ts passes at a median of 11.11 ms (load 4.1) and 7.84 ms (load 11), while the same board, cap 2000 and maxDepth 40 with the seeds times 2^60 (the same 2000 positions, same parents) takes 312.35 ms and 340.10 ms in redteam-RT-11-big-values.bench.ts. Unmutated at load 5.6 to 6: orbit.bench.ts 11.09 ms; seeds 0/1 2.91 ms; the seeds times 2^60 (the bigint loop) 21.68 ms. At load 11, the times-2^60 case measured 27.74 to 39.92 ms against 25. With the search loop as it was before b85ac0f restored (R-b85ac0f-search.patch, load 11), seeds 0/1 take 13.19 and 13.66 ms in bigint. The machine was never quiet (load 4 to 18), so absolute medians are indicative only. The F9 result does not depend on load.
reproduction: After `npm ci --prefer-offline` on this branch: `bash redteam/rt11-p4/bench-mutant.sh "$PWD" redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch`. It applies the patch, runs `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts` in packages/engine, reverts, and prints the medians: orbit benchmark under 25 ms and passing; RT-11 bench at over 300 ms and failing. Or by hand: `patch -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch`, then in packages/engine `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts orbit.bench; echo exit=$?` gives exit=0 and `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts redteam-RT-11; echo exit=$?` gives exit=1.
specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work' (the benchmark sentence); SPEC 5.5 'Orbits' (the 9 ms Big measurement it repeats); SPEC 5.1 E-9; RT-11 attack 24; CONTRACTS.md 3 (the benchmark: 'Big, median of seven runs, fails above 25 ms')
proposedFix: Make the 7.6 benchmark time the bigint loop, for example with the unit seeds times 2^60, which give the same 2000 positions. Or time both loops, each against 25 ms (redteam-RT-11-big-values.bench.ts does this). Record in DECISIONS.md which arithmetic the benchmark measures.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 [D] 'Main-thread work': 'its worst case, 2000 positions on a board with 12 nodes in `Big` arithmetic, took 9 ms in the measurement of section 5.5. A Vitest benchmark repeats that case (the 12-cycle with one chord, joining nodes 1 and 7, as in reference/bench_orbit.mjs) and fails above 25 ms (median of seven runs).' SPEC 5.5 says the 9 ms came from 'a direct implementation' with decimal-text keys. CONTRACTS.md 3 says '2000 positions, Big'. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4) and the 'MERGE: red-team round 1, residual fixes' entry record the engine change but not the benchmark.
refute.evidence: I read these at b9b8504. orbit.bench.ts asserts board.arith toBe Big, seeds the 12 bigint unit vectors on the 12-cycle with the 1-7 chord, and uses cap 2000, maxDepth 40, 7 runs, the median and 25 ms. So its inputs match 7.6 and CONTRACTS 3 word for word. search.ts:291-293 sends every Big board to searchOnNumbers while values are safe, so the timed call no longer does bigint arithmetic with decimal keys. reference/bench_orbit.mjs, the measurement 7.6 names, runs its 'Big' case through a bigint object with decimal-text keys. F9 (read as text) slows only lines 300-317, which these seeds never reach. Records: decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md (4) says 'orbitGraph on a SafeInt or Big board searches on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer', with 'Default used: none' and 'Reason: SPEC 7.6 and E-9'. It never names orbit.bench.ts or what the benchmark now times, and no other entry of that fragment does either. The DECISIONS.md MERGE entry for the round 1 residual fixes says 'orbitGraph on plain numbers with the bigint path from the same move; no result, cap or interface changed' and is also silent on the benchmark. The only other benchmark records are the P3 stage 3.1 MERGE entry (medians 19.75 and 21.60 ms, the bigint loop), the P4-A1 and P4 merge records of the medians, and the GATE G4 entry (median 12.61 ms). None records a change of the arithmetic measured. Nothing in the P4 'known and decided' list covers it. Possible counter-reading: E-2 says 'A board carries its arithmetic', and its [D] sentence 'writing the half-dozen core functions twice is acceptable; the tests do not care' would let 'in Big arithmetic' name the board, which the benchmark satisfies. But 7.6 and 5.5 tie 'that case' to bigint computation, so the text is ambiguous and nothing in it permits the benchmark to stop timing Big arithmetic. Phase: the benchmark is phase 3 (CONTRACTS 3, P3-A2), at or below G4.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 7.6 permits no other arithmetic for the benchmark and the 25 ms bound being met is not the claim; R2 is only partial, because the inputs, board arithmetic, cap, runs and threshold match 7.6 and CONTRACTS 3 literally, but whether 'in Big arithmetic' names the board (E-2) or the timed computation (5.5, bench_orbit.mjs) is an ambiguity for the owner, not a permission; R3 failed, because the benchmark is phase 3 at gate G4; R4 does not apply to a timing; R5 failed, because the 7.6 [D] text itself says Big and the residual-perf fragment (item 4) and the residual MERGE entry record the engine change but never what the benchmark now measures, so the finding's 'no record' part holds; R6 failed, because there is no open item in gate-G4.md or round 1; if true the claim falls under major ('a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong', or a missing required record).

title: T15.spec.ts checks the A-3 node names with a wildcard for the city number (residual sibling of P3-RT-11-08)
claim: The only check of T15's node names (A-3) accepts any digit as the city label and does not tie it to the button's data-node. T15 buttons that all said 'City 1, ...', or carried wrong labels, would pass.
expected: SPEC 7.5 A-3 fixes the name template ('City 2, population 1, mutation would raise it'). Each button's name should be compared whole, with the label read from its data-node, as P3-RT-11-08's fix did for A-4 sentences.
observed: `expect(await b.getAttribute('aria-label')).toMatch(/^City \d, population 1, mutation would change nothing$/)` runs in a loop over the four buttons of the square. No exact 'City <n>, ...' name appears anywhere in T15.spec.ts.
reproduction: `grep -n 'toMatch(/^City' site/tests/e2e/T15.spec.ts` prints line 132 as quoted. `grep -nE "'City [0-9], " site/tests/e2e/T15.spec.ts` prints nothing.
specRef: SPEC.md 7.5 A-3; CONTRACTS.md 5.3; RT-11 attack 33 (a loose comparison of a fixed sentence is minor per file)
proposedFix: Inside the loop, read data-node and compare toHaveAttribute('aria-label', `City ${label}, population 1, mutation would change nothing`).

refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because A-3 fixes the template, which includes the city label, with no qualifier; R2 failed, because the regex leaves the label free and ties it to no data-node, as the finding says; R3 failed, because T15 is phase 2 at G4; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because 7.5 A-3 is not [D] and nothing records a loose comparison; R6 failed, because round 1 saw the line only in a verifier's evidence and never recorded it as an open item; minor is the rubric's level for a test that could be stronger without being wrong (RT-11 attack 33).
